question.text: A compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced></math> with molar mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>108</mn><mi>g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> undergoes acetylation to give product with molar mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>192</mn><mi>g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The number of amino groups in the compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced></math> is ________.

solution.text:
The compounds like amines and alcohols undergo acetylation with acetyl chloride. During this reaction, one proton of amine or alcohol is replaced with one acetyl group(CH3CO-).

The molar mass of the acetyl group is 43 g/mol. The increase in molar mass due to one acetyl group is 43-1=42g/mol.

The molar mass of reactant is 108 g/mol. The molar mass of product is 192 g/mol.  The change in mass is 84.

Hence, the number of acetyl groups =8442=2
